feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: A rocky first press briefing for a rookie White House press secretary
entry.summary: Katie Zacharia's first White House press briefing was short and often halting. The new press secretary chosen by President Trump left a lot of unanswered questions, including some uncertainties about her own qualifications.

entry.title: Cornell's president has not resigned despite heavy scrutiny
entry.summary: The president of Cornell University, Michael Kotlikoff, is under fire over the university's handling of a gang rape at a fraternity party in 2024.

entry.title: In Kansas, a newly competitive Senate race tests limit of Trump's unpopular policies
entry.summary: Kansas voters could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century — and flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even in what could be a tough year for the GOP.

entry.title: 'They're stealing from the poor': A major source of SNAP fraud robs recipients of millions
entry.summary: Organized criminal rings target SNAP recipients because of the government program's outdated security features. But upgrading the tech costs money and states' SNAP budgets are getting squeezed.

entry.title: Labor Department to release latest inflation report
entry.summary: Higher energy prices, tied to the U.S. war with Iran, are driving up the overall cost-of-living. The Labor Department is set to deliver its latest inflation report this morning.

entry.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico prevail against White House — for now
entry.summary: A federal judge ruled late Tuesday that President Trump cannot ban news organizations from covering him at the White House because he does not like the nature of their coverage - at least, not until the matter goes to a formal trial.

entry.title: What an economics Nobel Prize winner knows about pricing
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang chats with Michael Woodford of Columbia University, who was one of two Americans awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.

entry.title: Naturalization in the U.S. is on the decline
entry.summary: The number of naturalization ceremonies for would-be American citizens is on the decline. This year, ceremonies have been canceled and citizenship applications face increased scrutiny and delays.

entry.title: Bipartisan group of senators call on Trump to rescind Russian diesel deal
entry.summary: Six Democratic and six Republican senators wrote a letter calling on President Trump to withdraw from his recent deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

entry.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
entry.summary: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.
